question: When can a neural system learn a fast same-class predictor by first learning a slower explicit procedure and then internalizing that procedure, and which curricula, architectures, and training distributions make this transition possible rather than producing a brittle shortcut?

key_findings.claim: Internalization is defined more strictly than trace shortening: a distinct parameterization in the same hypothesis class must agree with the original procedure on every input and run strictly faster.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 1 compares h_theta-prime directly with the composed slow procedure P(h_theta) on all x and requires a runtime inequality. Appendix B then introduces distributional internalization, which replaces all-input equality by an expected-loss tolerance and better matches the empirical studies.

anchors.section: Appendix B, Internalization processes: discussion and examples (Definition 2)

key_findings.claim: The semiautomata intervention progressively removes explicit state tokens while preserving a locally reusable transition computation; direct prediction and full CoT are the principal endpoints.
key_findings.evidence: The tasks are modular counters C_n plus noncommutative S_3 at horizons 15, 20, and 25. Main runs use depth 4, embedding 512, 128 heads, MLP width 2048, online AdamW with batch 128 and fresh sequences, 50,000 updates for counters and 200,000 for S_3, optimizer-state resets between stages, and 30 seeds per task-length configuration. Success means greater than 95% final-state accuracy, not exact agreement.

anchors.section: 3.1, Internalizing chain of thought over model width
Appendix E, Main configuration and seed protocol

key_findings.claim: Left-removal curricula often reach direct semiautomata solutions where end-to-end supervision fails, but success is probabilistic and falls with horizon and task.
key_findings.evidence: In Figure 2 at T=25, the plotted in-distribution success rates for internalization are 53%, 37%, 47%, 37%, 47%, 43%, 63%, and 3% for C_4 through C_10 and S_3 respectively; full CoT is 100% in those panels and end-to-end is 0%. These are 30-seed configuration-level rates under the paper's greater-than-95% threshold, not per-example accuracies or an all-input guarantee.

anchors.section: Figure 2, CoT versus E2E versus internalization
Appendix E, Experimental details and success-rate definition

key_findings.claim: The empirical semiautomata results do not satisfy the paper's own strict definition of exact internalization.
key_findings.evidence: The experiment declares success above 95% held-distribution accuracy, whereas Definition 1 requires agreement for every input. Moreover, Figures 1, 2, and 4 show OOD accuracy often degrading as CoT is removed, and the authors explicitly state on page 8 that the models fail to exactly internalize in the strict sense.

anchors.section: 3.2, The flip side of internalization: worse OOD performance

key_findings.claim: Width and attention-head count are more consistently favorable than additional depth, while the reported prime-order difficulty is an empirical pattern and conjectural explanation rather than a proved optimization law.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 3 and 8 compare 5M, 12M, and 20M isoparametric families and show higher success for wider, shallower configurations; Figure 9 shows gains from 1 to 16 or 32 heads at fixed embedding size. Figure 3's order sweep shows prime C_n tending to be harder than neighboring composite orders, but the text offers a representation-based hypothesis rather than an optimization theorem. Appendix E also reports that a right-removal curriculum gives 0/30 successes for the plotted C_3 and C_5 configurations, while C_7's plot annotation is not a clean 30-run estimate.

anchors.section: 3.3, Prime C_n are harder to internalize
Appendix E, Figure 8 and parameter-matched configurations
Appendix E, Figures 9-10 and curriculum comparison

key_findings.claim: The counter theorem establishes exact representational feasibility for cyclic semiautomata but does not show that gradient training finds the construction.
key_findings.evidence: The informal Theorem 1 and formal Theorem 3 construct a causal softmax Transformer for C_n when n factors into prime powers, with depth ceil(log2(T+1)), embedding dimension 2m+2, two heads of dimension m+2, MLP width 4 times the sum of the prime powers plus 4+2m, and bounded explicit weights. The proof uses Chinese remaindering, robust modular-addition ReLU networks, and sufficiently sharp softmax. No optimization result connects this construction to the empirical phase diagrams.

anchors.section: Appendix C.3, Exactness and bounded-weight proof conclusion

key_findings.claim: The parity theorem proves a complete curriculum trajectory only for a highly stylized one-layer causal linear-attention model.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2 takes step size eta=c/d, T=ceil(Cd) updates per phase, and batch size B at least C d^3 log(kT/delta), with fresh samples and probability at least 1-delta. Under the specified aligned initialization, fixed parity-specific piecewise-linear activation, entrywise rounding, and curriculum, it first learns next-token CoT and ends with exact direct k-parity on every Boolean input.

anchors.section: 4, Provable Internalization of Parities in 1-layer Transformers
Appendix D.1, Architecture, curriculum, and algorithm
Appendix D.3, Theorem 4 and Lemma 7 synthesis

key_findings.claim: Appendix-only qualifications materially narrow the parity theorem: zero initialization loses the phase-one explicit-CoT guarantee, and removing rounding is demonstrated only in one small experiment.
key_findings.evidence: A page-11 footnote says all-zero initialization still yields the final direct-parity conclusion but not the explicit phase-one CoT guarantee. Appendix D.4 omits rounding only for d=20, k=9, B=1024, eta=0.001 with an adaptive phase threshold; Figure 7 visualizes one learned attention trajectory. This does not establish rounding-free training in the theorem's general regime.

anchors.section: Appendix D.4, Experiments for learning parity with simplified Transformer

key_findings.claim: A noisy-parity MLP can learn from a curriculum or fixed mixture when target-only training remains at chance in the reported three-seed experiment.
key_findings.evidence: For bipolar d=25 inputs with hidden degree k=12 parity and label noise 0.1, the model expands inputs with k-1 hints and trains a two-hidden-layer width-2048 ReLU MLP (about 4.27M parameters) by SGD at 0.003, batch 64, for 600,000 steps. Figure 5 shows curriculum and uniform-stage mixture curves approaching the Bayes ceiling near 0.9 while direct training stays near 0.5; the paper provides curves and three-seed bands, not a tabulated terminal accuracy.

anchors.section: 5.1, Learning through Internalization with MLPs and Figure 5
5.2, From curricula to Positive Distribution Shift

key_findings.claim: The MLP construction is a generalized positive-distribution-shift example, not the strict covariate-shift setting of the predecessor framework.
key_findings.evidence: The original PDS setup keeps the input space and target labeling rule fixed while changing the covariate distribution. Here the curriculum changes the augmented context by replacing removed hints with independent random plus-or-minus-one noise, so Appendix F explicitly introduces generalized PDS to cover transformations between source and target examples. Calling the experiment ordinary covariate PDS would erase this distinction.

anchors.section: Appendix F.1, General Positive Distribution Shift

key_findings.claim: A fixed semiautomata mixture can support both direct answers and full CoT only because an answer-length token disambiguates the requested behavior.
key_findings.evidence: The mixture samples uniformly over all trace lengths but prepends LEN_L; at evaluation the same model is explicitly asked for length 1 or the full trace. Each minibatch is drawn from one selected stage and the comparisons use the same total number of samples. The result therefore does not demonstrate spontaneous reconciliation of conflicting unconditioned targets.

anchors.section: Appendix E.1, Learning Semiautomata with Mixture

key_findings.claim: The first-proof priority claim is narrow: the new element is a provable explicit-to-direct curriculum trajectory, not the first theory of parity with CoT or autoregressive CoT learning.
key_findings.evidence: The paper itself cites prior theory for learning autoregressive CoT and for parity with explicit intermediate supervision. Current primary records also show earlier work proving efficient parity learning with CoT. What this paper adds is a restricted gradient trajectory that continues through token removal to a direct predictor under its own same-class internalization definition.

method.core_idea: View an explicit multi-step generator and a faster direct predictor as two computations inside one hypothesis class, then use trace-removal curricula or favorable source distributions as a continuation path from the learnable slow computation to the otherwise hard fast one.
method.mechanism: The evidence has four distinct layers: GPT-style semiautomata experiments test curriculum direction and architecture; a constructive Chinese-remainder Transformer proves representation of cyclic counters; a one-layer linear-attention parity model proves a particular gradient-descent trajectory; and a noisy-parity MLP plus answer-length-conditioned semiautomata mixtures connect curricula to generalized positive distribution shift. These layers should not be treated as one shared optimization theorem.
assumptions: Definition 1 assumes the explicit procedure and direct predictor are instantiated by distinct parameters in the same hypothesis class and that procedure runtimes are meaningfully comparable.
Empirical semiautomata success substitutes greater-than-95% held-distribution accuracy for exact all-input equality and uses online synthetic data.
The main semiautomata conclusions depend on absolute positional embeddings, left or inductive curricula, optimizer resets, and selected shallow GPT-style architectures.
Theorem 3 is a constructive representational result with factorization-dependent width, logarithmic depth, sharp-softmax approximation, robust modular-addition MLPs, and explicitly chosen weights.

Theorem 2 assumes a one-layer causal linear-attention model, fixed parity-specific activation, aligned initialization, entrywise rounding, fresh large batches, phase-specific supervision, and full-batch gradient descent.
The noisy-parity MLP result uses bipolar inputs, random-noise replacement for absent hints, one d=25/k=12 task, label noise 0.1, and three seeds.
Mixture learning remains identifiable because the requested output length is encoded by LEN_L.

techniques.role: Deletes explicit state tokens stage by stage while retaining a learnable local transition structure.
Separates cyclic-group order, horizon, architecture, curriculum direction, and OOD sequence distribution.
Builds cyclic-counter Transformers from prime-power residues and a Chinese-remainder decoder.
Tracks a rounded full-batch trajectory from next-token parity CoT to exact direct parity.
Uses transformed hint distributions or their mixture to make noisy parity learnable.
Contrasts uniform training inputs with Binomial(n-1, 0.8) token sampling to reveal shortcut brittleness.

evaluations.setting: C_4-C_10 and S_3 semiautomata at T in {15,20,25}; main depth-4 GPT-style model with embedding 512, 128 heads, MLP width 2048; 30 seeds per task-length configuration; 50,000 online steps for counters and 200,000 for S_3; batch 128, AdamW 0.0003.
evaluations.metric: Fraction of seeds exceeding 95% final-state accuracy, response length, and ID/OOD accuracy.
evaluations.result: At T=25, full CoT is 100% successful and E2E is 0% across the plotted tasks, while left-curriculum internalization ranges from 3% on S_3 to 63% on C_10; the C_4-C_10 rates are 53%, 37%, 47%, 37%, 47%, 43%, and 63%.
evaluations.baseline: Full CoT supervision and direct end-to-end final-state supervision with the same architecture and sample budget.

evaluations.setting: Uniform-ID versus Binomial(n-1, 0.8)-OOD token sequences for C_2, C_3, C_5 and the broader Figure 2 task panel.
evaluations.metric: Final ID and OOD accuracy after successive CoT-token removal.
evaluations.result: ID success can remain near ceiling while OOD accuracy falls sharply; C_3 and C_5 remain OOD-weak even in deeper configurations, so successful held-distribution internalization is not procedural equivalence.
evaluations.baseline: The corresponding full-CoT checkpoint and held-distribution test accuracy.

evaluations.setting: Cyclic-counter sweeps over C_3-C_17, width 256 versus 2048, 5M/12M/20M isoparametric depth-width families, head counts 1/16/32, and left versus right curricula.
evaluations.metric: Thirty-seed internalization success rate above 95% ID accuracy.
evaluations.result: Wider/shallower and more-head configurations generally succeed more often; prime orders tend to be harder; right-removal records 0/30 for the clearly reported C_3 and C_5 settings while left-removal records 10/30 and 11/30.
evaluations.baseline: Neighboring composite orders, deeper matched-parameter models, fewer heads, and the opposite removal direction.

evaluations.setting: Constructed causal softmax Transformer for C_n over horizon T where n is decomposed into prime powers.
evaluations.metric: Exact state simulation and explicit architecture/weight bounds.
evaluations.result: Theorem 3 gives exact simulation with depth ceil(log2(T+1)), embedding 2m+2, two heads of dimension m+2, and MLP width 4 sum_j p_j^{v_j}+4+2m under its bounded-weight construction.
evaluations.baseline: Sequential T-step recurrence and generic finite-automaton constructions without the factorization-specific counter structure.

evaluations.setting: One-layer causal linear-attention parity model under Algorithm 2 with eta=c/d, T=ceil(Cd) updates per phase, B at least C d^3 log(kT/delta), fresh phase batches, rounding, and aligned initialization.
evaluations.metric: High-probability exact next-token CoT learning followed by exact direct k-parity on all {0,1}^d inputs.
evaluations.result: Theorem 2 guarantees both phases with probability at least 1-delta; the final one-pass predictor agrees exactly on every Boolean input.
evaluations.baseline: Direct parity learning without the explicit-to-implicit curriculum in the stylized model.

evaluations.setting: Rounding-free simplified-transformer illustration with d=20, k=9, batch 1024, eta=0.001, and adaptive phase advancement.
evaluations.metric: Curriculum accuracy and learned attention-weight evolution.
evaluations.result: The single small experiment succeeds without rounding and visually reorganizes attention across nine phases; no multi-scale or multi-seed generalization is supplied.

evaluations.setting: Two-hidden-layer width-2048 ReLU MLP on d=25, degree-12 noisy parity with 0.1 label noise; SGD 0.003, batch 64, 600,000 steps, 5,000-example evaluations, three seeds.
evaluations.metric: Target-distribution test accuracy versus training samples.
evaluations.result: Curriculum and uniform-stage mixture curves approach the 0.9 Bayes ceiling, while direct target-only training remains around chance; exact terminal values are not tabulated.
evaluations.baseline: Training directly on the target distribution with all hints replaced.

evaluations.setting: Semiautomata mixture over all answer lengths with LEN_L conditioning and equal total samples.
evaluations.metric: Fraction of seeds above 95% for direct answering and full-CoT generation.
evaluations.result: The conditioned mixture can train one model for both requested behaviors, with task-dependent success rates shown in Figure 5; it is not an unconditioned multi-target mixture.
evaluations.baseline: Stagewise curriculum and separately interpreted direct/full-CoT endpoints.

limitations: Author-stated: the strict all-input definition is not met by the semiautomata experiments; the authors explicitly identify the OOD failures as non-exact internalization.
Author-stated: the relationship between prime-power factorization and optimization difficulty is explanatory conjecture beyond the representation theorem.
Author-stated: the theory uses a simplified Transformer and the rounding-free result is only experimental.

Reviewer-identified: the representational construction, parity proof, GPT-style experiments, and MLP experiment use materially different architectures and objectives, so success in one layer of evidence does not validate the mechanism in another.
Reviewer-identified: the principal semiautomata metric is a thresholded 30-seed success fraction and can hide calibration, variance, and near-threshold behavior.
Reviewer-identified: OOD testing changes one synthetic token-frequency distribution; it does not establish robustness to length, transition, alphabet, or compositional shifts.

Reviewer-identified: the parity theorem depends on aligned initialization, a fixed task-specific activation, large fresh batches, full-batch updates, rounding, and linear rather than softmax attention.
Reviewer-identified: the MLP evidence is one d=25/k=12 noisy-parity problem with three seeds, and its strongest outcome is plot-only.
Reviewer-identified: the mixture result uses an explicit answer-length control token, so it cannot establish internalization from ambiguous direct and trace targets.

Reviewer-identified: the Appendix F construction broadens strict covariate PDS to transformations that change the augmented input, which weakens claims of direct equivalence to the predecessor framework.
failure_modes: A model crosses the held-distribution 95% threshold while implementing a frequency-sensitive shortcut that collapses under the Binomial OOD input distribution.
Direct end-to-end training stays at zero configuration-level success even though full CoT and the architecture's representational construction show the computation is available.

Right-side trace removal moves the position of the hard aggregate operation at every stage under absolute positional embeddings, and the curriculum records no successes in the cleanly reported C_3/C_5 comparisons.
Increasing depth at fixed parameter count reduces the width available for horizontal aggregation and can lower internalization probability.
Large prime-order counters require less favorable residue structure and empirically remain difficult despite neighboring composite orders succeeding.
The theoretical trajectory fails if initialization, activation regions, covariance concentration, rounding, or fresh-batch conditions do not hold.
An untagged mixture presents incompatible output lengths for the same input; LEN_L is required to make the demonstrated mixture identifiable.
Replacing missing MLP hints with random signs changes the input distribution and can make a claimed strict-PDS interpretation invalid.
reusable_insights: Define compilation-like learning with separate agreement, runtime, and distributional criteria; never infer exact internalization from shorter outputs plus held-distribution accuracy.
Curriculum direction should preserve a fixed-location local operation while gradually increasing the span of the aggregate computation.
Report seed-level success probability and per-example accuracy separately because thresholded run success measures optimization reliability, not task accuracy.
Use algebraic factorization to design architecture sweeps: state-space size alone can hide prime-power-dependent representation costs.
Keep representation, optimization, and generalization claims separate; a constructive exact circuit does not show gradient reachability, and a training proof does not show OOD procedural equivalence.
Treat source-target mixtures as identifiable only when the desired output mode is encoded or otherwise uniquely specified.
When relating curricula to distribution shift, state whether the intervention is covariate shift on a fixed input or a generalized transformation that changes the augmented example.
Audit appendix footnotes and experimental details before transferring theorem conditions to practice; here zero initialization and removal of rounding have materially narrower guarantees.
open_questions: Can a standard softmax Transformer with ordinary activations and initialization be proved to internalize parity without entrywise rounding?
What prospective statistic predicts whether a trace-removal curriculum will produce the same algorithm rather than an ID-only shortcut?
Does the prime-order effect survive controlled optimization studies that equalize representation width and initialization across group orders?
Can exact or exhaustive agreement be measured for the small semiautomata rather than using a 95% stochastic threshold?
Can an unconditioned mixture induce a single coherent fast computation without LEN_L or other output-mode metadata?
Which generalized-PDS transformations preserve the computational benefit while keeping the learned target identifiable?
Do the width-over-depth and head-count results transfer to natural reasoning tasks or modern RoPE-based architectures?
How should total training cost be incorporated when comparing an expensive curriculum with inference-time acceleration?

competitive_landscape.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Learning to Internalize CoT Step by Step
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest empirical predecessor progressively removes explicit CoT steps and demonstrates implicit multiplication and GSM8K reasoning.
competitive_landscape.difference: The present paper adopts essentially the same curriculum motif but adds a same-class formal definition, semiautomata structure/OOD audits, and a restricted parity training proof.

competitive_landscape.title: Implicit Chain of Thought Reasoning via Knowledge Distillation
competitive_landscape.relationship: It moves explicit horizontal CoT into vertical hidden-state computation and is a direct predecessor for faster implicit reasoning.
competitive_landscape.difference: It distills teacher hidden states across layers rather than proving a trace-removal gradient trajectory within the paper's same-class procedure definition.

competitive_landscape.title: Distilling System 2 into System 1
competitive_landscape.relationship: It compiles slower System-2 procedures into cheaper direct generations and directly overlaps the inference-time motivation.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies practical output distillation rather than exact same-class procedural agreement, semiautomata curricula, or parity optimization.

competitive_landscape.title: Implicit Reasoning in Transformers is Reasoning through Shortcuts
competitive_landscape.relationship: It directly tests whether implicit reasoning generalizes or exploits fixed-pattern shortcuts.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is primarily a negative empirical audit; this paper supplies curricula and a formal lens but independently reproduces the same shortcut concern through OOD degradation.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Provably Solve Parity Efficiently with Chain of Thought
competitive_landscape.relationship: This is the closest theoretical parity predecessor, proving efficient one-layer Transformer learning with explicit intermediate parity states.
competitive_landscape.difference: It does not continue a learned model through progressive CoT removal to a direct predictor; therefore the new priority can only concern that explicit-to-direct internalization trajectory, not parity-with-CoT theory broadly.

competitive_landscape.title: Positive Distribution Shift as a Framework for Understanding Tractable Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: The coauthored predecessor formalizes computationally helpful training distributions and directly motivates the paper's PDS interpretation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Its primary formal setting is covariate shift on fixed inputs and labels; the present hint-removal construction changes augmented examples and consequently requires the broader generalized-PDS definition in Appendix F.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
competitive_landscape.relationship: It proves low-depth Transformer shortcut representations for finite automata and empirically studies their learnability and brittleness.
competitive_landscape.difference: The present paper studies a curriculum between recurrent traces and direct shortcuts, plus factorization-specific cyclic counters; it does not originate low-depth automata shortcut representation or the associated brittleness concern.

competitive_landscape.title: A Theory of Learning with Autoregressive Chain of Thought
competitive_landscape.relationship: It formalizes observed versus latent autoregressive CoT learning and analyzes sample and computational complexity.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies learnability of iterated time-invariant generators, not a parameter trajectory that progressively deletes an already learned trace to yield a faster direct computation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first provable analysis of successful internalization and a unified view linking CoT-token removal, semiautomata shortcuts, and positive distribution shift.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper contributes a strict same-class/runtime definition, unusually broad semiautomata curriculum and OOD sweeps, a factorization-aware exact counter construction, and Theorem 2's high-probability gradient trajectory from explicit parity CoT to exact one-pass parity under restrictive conditions.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the explicit-to-direct parity trajectory plus the synthesis of curriculum, representation, and generalized PDS evidence. The gradual-removal algorithm is directly preceded by arXiv:2405.14838; parity learning with CoT is directly preceded by arXiv:2410.08633 and PMLR v291; and automata shortcuts are preceded by arXiv:2210.10749. Accordingly, 'first provable analysis' should be read narrowly as the first proof under this paper's internalization definition and stylized training algorithm, not as first theory of implicit CoT, automata shortcuts, or parity with CoT.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification completed against the exact pinned arXiv v1 source on 2026-08-23. I independently read and checked all 43 PDF pages, including every figure and caption, the related-work appendix, Definitions 2-4, the full semiautomata construction and proof, the full parity proof and rounding-free appendix experiment, all semiautomata configuration plots, and both generalized-PDS appendices. This revision corrects shifted appendix labels (B/C/D/E/F rather than the prior A/B/C/D labels), distinguishes informal Theorem 1 from formal Theorem 3, records the exact Theorem 2 batch/step conditions, treats prime difficulty and OOD equivalence conservatively, notes the zero-initialization and no-rounding qualifications, identifies random-sign hint replacement and LEN_L conditioning, and avoids reading exact terminal MLP values from curves.
